assessment.subject: degarelix (GnRH antagonist)
assessment.object: leuprolide (GnRH agonist), cardiovascular safety in prostate cancer
assessment.claim_summary: Randomized open-label trial (PRONOUNCE) found no significant difference in major adverse cardiovascular events at 12 months between degarelix and leuprolide in prostate cancer patients with atherosclerotic disease.

assessment.subject: irritable bowel syndrome treatment
assessment.claim_summary: Narrative review summarizing recent pharmacological and nonpharmacological treatment options for irritable bowel syndrome; presents no new empirical result.

assessment.subject: Melanotan II (MT II) use
assessment.claim_summary: Qualitative thematic analysis of UK/Ireland online forum posts characterizing motivations for Melanotan II use and its self-reported side-effect profile; concludes clinicians should be aware of associated hazards.

assessment.subject: hypoactive sexual desire disorder in women
assessment.claim_summary: Clinical overview of hypoactive sexual desire disorder in women covering physiology, assessment, diagnosis, and treatment (including flibanserin and bremelanotide); no new empirical result.

assessment.subject: age-related macular degeneration therapeutic candidates
assessment.claim_summary: Review discussing potential therapeutic candidates and their cytoprotective mechanisms for age-related macular degeneration; no empirical result reported.

assessment.subject: semaglutide (Wegovy, GLP-1 receptor agonist)
assessment.object: placebo / other antidiabetic drugs, weight loss
assessment.claim_summary: Literature review of the SUSTAIN, PIONEER, and STEP trial programs concluding semaglutide has superior weight-loss efficacy versus placebo and other agents, supporting FDA approval of Wegovy.

assessment.subject: cagrilintide (long-acting amylin analogue)
assessment.claim_summary: Phase 2 dose-finding randomized double-blind trial: once-weekly cagrilintide produced significantly greater weight loss than placebo (up to 10.8% vs 3.0%) and greater than liraglutide 3.0 mg at the 4.5 mg dose over 26 weeks; well tolerated.
assessment.magnitude: 6.0-10.8% weight loss vs 3.0% placebo; 4.5mg 10.8% vs liraglutide 9.0%

assessment.subject: semaglutide 2.4 mg/week
assessment.claim_summary: Review of semaglutide 2.4 mg/week for obesity reporting approximately 15% weight loss at 68 weeks with cardiometabolic and functional improvements; described as the largest weight loss of any obesity medication to date.

assessment.subject: bremelanotide (melanocortin receptor agonist)
assessment.object: placebo, female hypoactive sexual desire disorder
assessment.claim_summary: Narrative review of bremelanotide for female hypoactive sexual desire disorder reporting improved desire, arousal, and orgasm scores versus placebo; described as a promising treatment.

assessment.subject: GHK / GHK-Cu peptide
assessment.object: aging, skin remodeling, wound healing, cognition
assessment.claim_summary: Review summarizing in vitro and in vivo evidence that GHK and its copper chelate have anti-inflammatory and tissue-remodeling effects, with preliminary mouse data suggesting partial reversal of cognitive impairment; argues for further study.

assessment.subject: bremelanotide
assessment.claim_summary: Integrated review of bremelanotide safety across the phase 1-3 clinical development program (3500 subjects) reporting adverse events (e.g., nausea 40.0% vs 1.3% placebo) as mostly mild-to-moderate, with caution advised in cardiovascular-risk patients.

assessment.subject: melanotan-II (MC3/4R agonist) in nucleus accumbens
assessment.claim_summary: Controlled mouse experiment: melanotan-II microinjected into the nucleus accumbens significantly decreased food consumption and motivation to obtain food without inducing aversion or altering metabolic rate.

assessment.subject: neoadjuvant degarelix + apalutamide
assessment.object: degarelix + placebo, high-risk prostate cancer (radical prostatectomy)
assessment.claim_summary: Randomized placebo-controlled phase II trial (ARNEO): neoadjuvant degarelix plus apalutamide before prostatectomy achieved a higher minimal-residual-disease rate than degarelix alone (38% vs 9.1%, RR 4.2).

assessment.subject: Selank (tuftsin peptide analogue)
assessment.object: morphine withdrawal in rats; diazepam comparator
assessment.claim_summary: Controlled rat study: a single 0.3 mg/kg dose of Selank reduced the total morphine-withdrawal index by 39.6% and raised the tactile threshold 9-fold, slightly less than diazepam.
assessment.magnitude: 39.6% reduction in withdrawal index; 9-fold higher tactile threshold

assessment.subject: setmelanotide (MC4R agonist)
assessment.object: placebo, Bardet-Biedl and Alstrom syndrome obesity
assessment.claim_summary: Phase 3 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial: setmelanotide significantly reduced bodyweight in Bardet-Biedl syndrome (32.3% reached >=10% loss at 52 weeks) but results were inconclusive in Alstrom syndrome.

assessment.subject: semaglutide and liraglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonists)
assessment.claim_summary: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of 23 RCTs (11,545 patients): all GLP-1 receptor agonists outperformed placebo for weight loss, with semaglutide 2.4 mg best (-12.47 kg) but the highest total adverse-event incidence.

assessment.subject: subcutaneous semaglutide
assessment.claim_summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 4 RCTs (3,613 patients): semaglutide produced an -11.85% weight reduction vs placebo, with higher risks of gastrointestinal and serious adverse events and treatment discontinuation.

assessment.subject: tirzepatide (dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist)
assessment.object: placebo, semaglutide 1mg and other agents; T2DM and obesity
assessment.claim_summary: Review of the SURPASS and SURMOUNT-1 programs reporting tirzepatide (5-15 mg weekly) reduced HbA1c by 1.87-3.02% and bodyweight by 5.4-12.9 kg in T2DM and 16.5-22.4% in obesity, with tolerability similar to GLP-1 agonists.

assessment.subject: tirzepatide (Mounjaro, dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist)
assessment.claim_summary: Overview of tirzepatide (Mounjaro) summarizing five SURPASS trials that demonstrated potent glucose lowering and weight loss with adverse effects comparable to GLP-1 receptor agonists.

assessment.subject: Prader-Willi syndrome therapies (hyperphagia/obesity)
assessment.claim_summary: Review discussing the status of clinical trials of agents (e.g., setmelanotide, DCCR, oxytocin, GLP-1 agonists) for hyperphagia and obesity in Prader-Willi syndrome; no synthesized empirical result.

assessment.subject: tirzepatide 15 mg
assessment.object: semaglutide 1mg / placebo; appetite, energy intake, body composition in T2DM
assessment.claim_summary: Secondary analysis of a randomized double-blind trial: tirzepatide 15 mg significantly reduced bodyweight and fat mass versus placebo and semaglutide and reduced appetite versus placebo, but appetite/energy-intake differences did not fully explain weight loss.

assessment.subject: anti-PD-1 plus ADT/PI3K inhibitor (immunometabolic combination)
assessment.object: PTEN/p53-deficient prostate cancer (mouse models and patient samples)
assessment.claim_summary: Preclinical study in PTEN/p53-deficient mouse prostate cancer: adding anti-PD-1 to ADT plus PI3K inhibition produced an approximately 3-fold increase in anticancer response via reduced lactate and macrophage reactivation; supported by patient single-cell RNA-seq correlations.
